the expression of 4 of 6 CCN family genes is regulated by glycolytic activity, and that the regulation of CCNs by energy metabolism is a novel mechanism underlying the crosstalk of CCN2 with other CCNs in chondroprotection.

the CCN family members are regulated by the glycolysis in the chondrocyte, which regulation would have an impact on the pathogenesis of osteoarthritis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CCN2 and 3 are the 2 most important members in chondrogenesis, and their expression is tightly regulated by the metabolic state of chondrocyte.
glycolysis is the major energy metabolic process that regulates the expression of the CCN2 and 3 genes in chondrogenic cells.
the glycolytic activity is critical for the regulation of CCNs in chondroblasts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glycolysis is a major regulator of the CCN genes in chondrogenic cells.
the expression of CCNs in chondroblastic cells is tightly regulated by glycolysis, which is a key metabolic process in those cells.
the CCN family members are reciprocally regulated by the metabolic activity, and the metabolic regulation of CCN proteins may be a common theme in the CCN family.
